statusText: EA_ON - Tail 15 of 100 in the low band, below the watch and block thresholds; Stress 72 high; Confidence 87 high.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON with Tail at 15. The futures reopen after the CME maintenance pause is orderly and two-sided: NQ trades 29,268.75, up 0.08%, inside a 25.5-point band from 29,251.25 to 29,276.75, with no directional efficiency and no extension after a failed retracement. That follows a cash close that itself granted mean reversion, the Nasdaq-100 settling at 28,937.84 after being bought back from a marginal new low at 28,899.43, while VIX closed at 17.20, well below its 18.03 session high. Stress remains high at 72 because the backdrop has not improved: the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.01% after a 5.045% intraday high, the highest since 2007, the 2-year is 4.67% and WTI is $105.45 with Brent $108.39 following the Saudi East-West pipeline outage. Internals conflict, with semiconductors higher and megacaps lower, which reduces directional conviction rather than adding path risk. A live FOMC decision with a Summary of Economic Projections is scheduled for 18:00Z on 16 September and the press conference from 18:30Z, with a 25 basis-point hike priced near 93%; that sequence is the published danger window of 18:00Z to 19:30Z and the only part of this horizon mapping to the block band. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ reopens after the CME pause and trades 29,268.75, up 0.08% in a 25-point two-sided band, easing Tail to 15 while Stress stays high at 72 with the 10-year at 5.01%, WTI at $105.45 and a live FOMC decision due Wednesday at 18:00Z
body:
Globex has reopened after the daily CME maintenance pause and NQ futures trade 29,268.75, up 22.00 points or 0.08%, inside a session range of 29,251.25 to 29,276.75. That 25.5-point band is the structural observation that carries this hour. Price is trading on both sides of the reopen reference with no directional efficiency, no extension after a failed retracement and no pinning near a session extreme, which is the opposite of the persistent one-way structure that defines a pathological path. The reopen also follows a cash close that granted mean reversion: the Nasdaq-100 settled at 28,937.84, down 189.32 points or 0.65% from a 29,127.16 previous close, after opening at 29,100.16 and trading a 28,899.43 to 29,142.80 range. The index printed a marginal new low late in the session, was bought back from it and settled roughly 38 points above it. Volatility agrees. VIX finished at 17.20, up 0.10 points or 0.58% on the day but well under its 18.03 session high and close to the 16.79 low, so volatility never confirmed the price low. Broader tape internals were two-sided rather than aligned: semiconductors closed mostly higher, with QCOM up 4.25% and AMD up 2.21%, while megacaps were predominantly lower, AMZN down 2.02% and MSFT down 1.68%, and software indices fell more than 1%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress rather than Tail.

The pressure in this regime sits in rates and energy, and it has not eased. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.01% after a 5.045% intraday print, a fifth consecutive daily rise and the highest level since 2007; the 2-year is 4.67%, its highest since mid-2024, and the 30-year is 5.37%. Crude remains the second channel, with WTI at $105.45, up 4.38%, and Brent at $108.39 after drone strikes from Iraqi territory damaged pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline on 10-11 September, forcing a shutdown of the route that carries about 5 million barrels a day to Yanbu while the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted and the U.S. naval blockade is in force. Energy-driven inflation and an expanded term premium are the reported causes of the bond selloff, and both remain unresolved.

The dominant scheduled feature of this horizon is Wednesday's FOMC decision at 18:00Z, accompanied by a Summary of Economic Projections and a press conference from 18:30Z. Markets price roughly a 93% probability of a 25 basis-point increase to 3.75-4.00%, which would be the first hike since 2023, after August core CPI rose 0.3% month-on-month and headline CPI reached 3.4% year-on-year. August retail sales, the Empire State index and the New York Fed services survey print earlier that day at 12:30Z. The decision sequence is structurally multi-stage: statement, projections, then a question period during which the yield reaction can drive a delayed second equity leg. That mechanism, not the size of any surprise, is why the 18:00Z and 19:00Z slots are the only part of this horizon projected into the block band and why the published danger window is 18:00Z to 19:30Z on 16 September. No FOMC outcome is assumed here; the pricing is market expectation, not a result.

Tail is therefore assessed at 15, in the low band, mapping to EA_ON and green. The mapped state rests on live evidence of an orderly, extremely narrow futures reopen with two-sided trade, a cash close that was bought back from its own low, and volatility that declined relative to its session high. Stress is 72, in the high band, because the yield, energy and event backdrop is unchanged and demanding. Confidence is 87 on a live NQ quote, verified cash and volatility closes, verified 2-year, 10-year and 30-year yields, verified WTI and Brent levels, a verified seven-day U.S. calendar and verified reporting on the rate path and the pipeline outage. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail ranged from 14 to 25 and entered the block band in exactly one hour, the 08:00Z European-morning slot. The overnight stretch from 22:00Z through 03:00Z was the calmest of the cycle, with Tail between 14 and 16 as the range compressed, and 05:00Z was the first lift, recorded as trend-down at 24. Through the Tuesday U.S. session Tail rebuilt from 18 at 11:00Z to a 24 peak at 15:00Z as the index worked lower and the 10-year pushed above 5%, then eased to 20 by 18:00Z, ticked to 21 at 19:00Z on the power-hour retest of the session low and fell to 17 for the closing and maintenance-pause hours once that low was bought back. Stress held in the high band for the entire U.S. session, between 70 and 77, and Confidence stayed between 86 and 89 throughout. The cycle was one of persistent cross-asset pressure assessed on consistently good evidence rather than a single disorderly episode.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail starts at 15 for the current reopen hour, where the observed 25-point two-sided band is the evidence, then eases to a horizon floor of 14 across the 23:00Z to 02:00Z Asian stretch that matched the calmest hours of the published lookback. From the European pre-market it rebuilds stepwise, reaching 18 at 05:00Z and crossing into the watch band at 07:00Z, and peaks for the European morning at 21 in the 08:00Z slot that carried the prior cycle's only block-band reading. The late-European lull returns it to 19 before the data block: 22 for the 12:00Z hour containing retail sales and the Empire State survey, then 24 for the 13:00Z hour that carries both the data digestion and the 13:30Z U.S. cash open, the highest pre-decision reading on the horizon. After a mid-session ease to 21 the final approach lifts it from 22 at 16:00Z to 24 at 17:00Z as pre-event liquidity thins. The horizon tops at 28 in the 18:00Z slot containing the FOMC statement, the Summary of Economic Projections and the start of the press conference, and holds at 26 through the 19:00Z question period; those two slots are the only part of the horizon mapping to the block band and they bracket the published danger window of 18:00Z to 19:30Z. The final cash hour returns to 23 on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly once the projections are absorbed, and the post-close hour settles at 20. Confidence decays from 87 to 59 across the horizon as verified live evidence gives way to conditional reasoning.
